To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the similarity between automatically generated topic distributions can be estimated reliably using distributional semantic and knowledge-based methods, and that the word probability distributions previously used to compare topics are not suitable for this purpose.

the distributional similarity measures outperformed all others in terms of correlation with human judgements, and that the knowledge-based measures were competitive with the distributional measures, and in some cases outperformed them, when used with the appropriate similarity metric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of measuring the similarity of automatically generated topics, which has been a long-standing problem in text mining and information retrieval.
the problem of measuring the similarity between topics that have been identified automatically by topic modelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distribution-based measures are the most appropriate to use, and that the other measures are not as appropriate to use.
the best performing similarity measures for automatically generated topics were the knowledge-based measures.
the word probability distribution methods are the worst performing methods, and that the knowledge-based methods are the best performing methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best performing methods are based on the distributional semantics approach and the knowledge-based measures.
the word distribution similarity measures, which are the basis for most of the existing approaches to the problem, are not the best ones.
, in order to compare the semantic similarity of topics, it is necessary to go beyond the word probabilities and consider the semantics of the topic words and their relations with each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when measuring the similarity between topics, we should not rely solely on their lexical content, but should also take into account the semantic relationships between their terms.
the similarity of automatically generated topics is best estimated by using distributional similarity measures based on word vectors.
the use of knowledgebased measures can improve the performance of topic similarity measures, and that distributional measures based on word vectors can also be useful.
